t: Under Section 146 of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988, which of the following vehicles is exempt from the requirement of compulsory third-party insurance?
o: Vehicles used exclusively in rural areas
Vehicles owned by the Central Government or State Government used for purposes not connected with any commercial enterprise, where a fund is maintained as per the Act
e: Section 146(2) exempts vehicles owned by the Central or State Government (not used for commercial enterprise) and other specified vehicles, subject to the Government maintaining a fund for compensation.

t: Under the IRDAI (Insurance Advertisements and Disclosure) Regulations 2021, an advertisement which does not include any information on the product (e.g. only brand name, logo, awards) is termed:
o: An institutional advertisement, which need not be filed with IRDAI
e: Institutional advertisements promoting only the insurer's name/brand without product details are distinguished from insurance advertisements and are exempt from filing.

t: Under the PPHI Regulations 2024, a life insurer must pay maturity claims, survival benefits and annuities:
o: Within 30 days of the due date
On the due date itself, the insurer having initiated action in advance
Within 15 days of receipt of a claim form
Within 45 days of the due date
e: The regulations require maturity, survival benefit and annuity payments to be made on the due date, with the insurer initiating action in advance.

t: Under the Consumer Protection Act 2019, an appeal against an order of the National Commission (in its original jurisdiction) lies to:
e: Section 67 provides that an appeal from an order of the National Commission made in exercise of its original jurisdiction lies to the Supreme Court within 30 days.

t: Under the Employees' Compensation Act 1923, compensation for death or permanent total disablement is calculated with reference to the monthly wages of the employee, with a wage ceiling for computation currently fixed at:
e: The Central Government notified Rs 15,000 per month (from 2020) as the wage ceiling for computing compensation under Section 4 of the EC Act.

t: Under the IRDAI (Insurance Surveyors and Loss Assessors) Regulations 2015, the licence/membership of a surveyor is granted by:
o: The Indian Institute of Insurance Surveyors and Loss Assessors (IIISLA) only
IRDAI, with the applicant required to be a member of IIISLA
e: IRDAI issues the surveyor licence after the applicant completes the prescribed practical training and examination, and membership of IIISLA is a condition for licensing.

t: Under current IRDAI health insurance norms (2024), coverage of AYUSH treatments (Ayurveda, Yoga, Unani, Siddha, Homeopathy) in health policies:
o: Is restricted to 10% of sum insured
Is available only in Government hospitals
Must be offered without any sub-limit, treating AYUSH at par with allopathic treatment, subject to policy terms
e: IRDAI directed insurers to cover AYUSH treatments without restrictions and at par with other treatments, so that policyholders have freedom of choice of treatment system.

t: Under IRDAI's solvency framework, the 'Available Solvency Margin' (ASM) is defined as:
o: The excess of the value of assets over the value of liabilities, computed as per IRDAI's valuation norms
e: ASM is the excess of admissible assets over liabilities (including policy liabilities and provisions); the solvency ratio is ASM divided by Required Solvency Margin, which must be at least 1.5.

t: Under the IMF Regulations 2015, the geographical area of operation of an Insurance Marketing Firm was originally restricted to:
o: One district (later relaxed to allow more districts/an aspirational district within a State)
e: IMFs were registered for one district; IRDAI subsequently relaxed the norms, allowing operation in additional districts and offering incentives for aspirational districts.

t: Under the Outsourcing Regulations 2017, the insurer must constitute an Outsourcing Committee comprising:
o: Key management persons including the CRO, CFO and CCO (or equivalents), with the Chief Risk Officer as a member
e: The regulations require an Outsourcing Committee of senior executives (CRO, CFO, CCO, etc.) to approve outsourcing arrangements under a board-approved outsourcing policy.

t: The IRDA Act 1999 was enacted following the recommendations of which committee?
e: The Malhotra Committee under R.N. Malhotra recommended opening the sector to private players and setting up an independent regulator, leading to the IRDA Act 1999.

t: Under the Insurance Ombudsman Rules 2017 (as amended in 2021), complaints may be filed by:
o: Only through the insurer's grievance officer
Only the policyholder in person at the Ombudsman office
The policyholder, nominee, legal heir or assignee, including electronically through the online Complaint Management System
e: The 2021 amendment enabled electronic filing of complaints and video-conference hearings; complaints may be filed by the policyholder, legal heirs, nominees or assignees.

t: Section 27 of the Insurance Act 1938 requires a life insurer to invest and keep invested its controlled fund in which of the following?
o: Only in equity shares of listed companies
Entirely in fixed deposits of scheduled commercial banks
At least 60% in real estate and infrastructure
At least 25% in Government securities and the balance in any approved securities as prescribed
e: Section 27(1) requires every life insurer to invest not less than the prescribed percentage of its controlled fund in Government securities and approved securities, with the balance as per IRDAI investment regulations.

t: Section 42D of the Insurance Act 1938 empowers IRDAI to issue licences to:
o: Insurance intermediaries or insurance agents such as brokers, corporate agents and other intermediaries as regulated
e: Section 42D (as substituted) covers registration of insurance intermediaries, including brokers, corporate agents, web aggregators and others, subject to IRDAI regulations.

t: A TPA is appointed by an insurer. Under the TPA Regulations 2016, who bears responsibility for the TPA's service deficiency towards the policyholder?
o: The insurer, who is ultimately responsible for the services rendered by its TPA
e: The insurer remains responsible for the services of the TPA it engages; the agreement between insurer and TPA must define service levels, and the insurer cannot disclaim liability.

t: Under the PPHI Regulations 2024, a life insurer must settle a death claim requiring investigation within:
o: 45 days from the date of receipt of intimation of claim
90 days from the date of death
e: The 2024 regulations require a death claim warranting investigation to be settled within 45 days from the date of intimation; claims not requiring investigation within 15 days.

t: Under the current threshold notified by IRDAI (2020 amendment), appointment of a licensed surveyor is mandatory for a motor insurance claim where the loss exceeds:
e: The thresholds were raised in 2020 to Rs 50,000 for motor claims and Rs 1 lakh for other classes; losses below these may be settled without a licensed surveyor.

t: Under Section 25 of the IRDA Act 1999, the Insurance Advisory Committee is chaired by:
o: The Chairperson of IRDAI, with members of the Authority as ex-officio members
The Secretary General of the Life Insurance Council
The Finance Secretary, Government of India
e: Section 25 provides that the Chairperson and members of the Authority are ex-officio members of the Insurance Advisory Committee, which the Chairperson of IRDAI heads.

t: The Tariff Advisory Committee (TAC) constituted under Section 64U of the Insurance Act 1938 historically performed which function before it was wound up?
o: Managing the motor third party pool
Controlling and regulating premium rates, terms and conditions for general insurance business
e: The TAC controlled rates and terms for general insurance; with detariffing from 2007 it lost relevance and was finally dissolved by the Insurance Laws (Amendment) Act 2015.

t: Under Section 38 of the Insurance Act 1938 (as amended in 2015), when is an assignment or transfer of a life policy considered effective as against the insurer?
o: From the date the policyholder signs the assignment deed, regardless of notice
Only after a court decree confirming the assignment
Only after the nominee consents in writing
From the date the insurer receives written notice of the assignment along with the instrument or its certified copy
e: Section 38(5) provides that an assignment is operative against the insurer only from the date the notice of assignment, with the endorsement or instrument (or certified copy), is delivered to the insurer.

t: Under Section 149 of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988 (as substituted in 2019), on receipt of information about an accident from the police, the insurer must:
o: Wait for the Tribunal to decide the claim
Immediately pay Rs 5 lakh to the victim
Designate an officer to settle the claim and make an offer to the claimant within 30 days; if accepted, pay within 30 days of settlement
Refer the claim to the Insurance Ombudsman
e: Section 149 (2019 amendment) requires the insurer's designated officer to make a settlement offer within 30 days, failing which the claimant may approach the Claims Tribunal under Section 166.

t: Following the 2015 amendment to the Insurance Act 1938, a foreign reinsurer may carry on reinsurance business in India through a branch provided it has a minimum net owned fund of:
e: Section 2(9)/6 read with IRDAI regulations require a foreign reinsurer setting up a branch in India to have a minimum net owned fund of Rs 5,000 crore.

t: Under Section 3 of the Insurance Act 1938, IRDAI may cancel the certificate of registration of an insurer in which of the following situations?
o: If the insurer declares a dividend to its shareholders
If the insurer fails to comply with the provisions of Section 64VA relating to solvency or carries on business other than insurance business
If the insurer changes its registered office within India
If the insurer appoints a new Chief Executive Officer without prior approval of the Life Insurance Council
e: Section 3(4) lists grounds for cancellation including failure to maintain solvency margin under Section 64VA, carrying on business other than insurance business, and default in complying with Authority directions.

t: An Insurance Repository, approved by IRDAI, performs which function?
o: Maintains policies in electronic form in an e-Insurance Account (eIA) on behalf of policyholders
Pays claims on behalf of insurers
e: Insurance Repositories (such as NSDL, CDSL, CAMS, Karvy repositories) hold electronic policies in e-Insurance Accounts and service them, under IRDAI's repository guidelines.

t: Under the EoM Regulations 2023, an insurer that exceeds the expenses of management limit must:
o: Pay a penalty of Rs 25 crore
Submit a board-approved business plan to IRDAI showing how it will achieve compliance within a specified period, and may be directed to charge the excess to shareholders' funds
e: Insurers exceeding the EoM limit must seek forbearance with a glide path/business plan approved by the board; the excess is to be charged to shareholders' account.

t: IRDAI has notified the obligatory cession to the Indian reinsurer (GIC Re) for general insurance business. For the current notified period (from FY 2022-23 onwards), the percentage is:
e: The obligatory cession to GIC Re was reduced from 5% to 4% from 1 April 2022 and has continued at 4% under subsequent notifications.

t: Under Section 5 of the IRDA Act 1999, a whole-time member of IRDAI (other than the Chairperson) holds office for a term of:
o: Five years or until age 65, whichever is earlier
Three years or until age 60, whichever is earlier
Five years or until age 62, whichever is earlier
e: Section 5 provides that whole-time members hold office for five years and are eligible for reappointment, but not beyond age 62; the Chairperson's age limit is 65.

t: Under the Insurance Ombudsman Rules 2017, an Ombudsman must pass an award within how long of receipt of the complaint?
e: Rule 17 requires the Ombudsman to dispose of the complaint and pass an award within three months of receipt of all requirements from the complainant.

t: The Insurance (Amendment) Act 2021 raised the foreign investment limit to 74% but retained which safeguard, as later specified in the Indian Insurance Companies (Foreign Investment) Amendment Rules 2021?
o: A majority of directors and key management persons must be resident Indian citizens, and at least one among the Chairperson, MD and CEO must be a resident Indian citizen
All board meetings must be held in India
Dividend repatriation is prohibited for 10 years
Foreign promoters must hold at least 51% permanently
e: The 2021 Rules require that for insurers with foreign investment, a majority of directors and KMPs be resident Indian citizens, with at least one of Chairperson/MD/CEO being a resident Indian citizen.

t: Under the IRDAI POSP framework, who is responsible for conducting the examination and appointing a POSP?
o: The insurer or intermediary (such as broker, corporate agent or IMF) who engages the POSP, after in-house training and examination
The Insurance Institute of India exclusively
e: The POSP is trained and examined (15 hours) by the engaging insurer or intermediary, who appoints and is accountable for the POSP; details are reported to IRDAI.

t: Under the Public Liability Insurance Act 1991, the relief for death of a person caused by an accident involving a hazardous substance (no-fault liability) is payable by:
o: The owner, on a no-fault basis, with the amount of relief specified in the Schedule to the Act and the claim adjudicated by the Collector
e: Section 3 imposes no-fault liability on the owner to give relief as per the Schedule (Rs 25,000 for death plus medical expenses), and claims are made to the Collector under Section 6.

t: Under Section 14(2)(e) of the IRDA Act 1999, IRDAI is empowered to levy:
o: Fees and other charges for carrying out the purposes of the Act
e: Section 14(2)(e) empowers the Authority to levy fees and other charges, such as registration and renewal fees from insurers and intermediaries.

t: Under the Marine Insurance Act 1963, a 'constructive total loss' arises where:
o: The subject matter is physically destroyed
The subject matter is reasonably abandoned because its actual total loss appears unavoidable, or the cost of recovery/repair would exceed its value when recovered
The ship is delayed by more than 30 days
e: Section 60 defines constructive total loss, and under Section 61 the assured may treat it as a partial loss or abandon the subject matter to the insurer and claim a total loss.

t: Under the Web Aggregators Regulations 2017, an insurer may pay a web aggregator a fee for each lead that converts into a policy. Which statement is correct regarding display of products?
o: Web aggregators must display products in a fair and unbiased manner, without rating or ranking based on remuneration, and must not display advertisements of any insurer
Web aggregators may sell only life insurance products
Web aggregators must display only products of insurers with whom they have no agreement
Web aggregators may rank products based on the commission payable
e: The regulations require unbiased comparative display and prohibit web aggregators from carrying insurer advertisements or ranking products on the basis of remuneration.

t: Under the Consumer Protection Act 2019 read with the 2021 Jurisdiction Rules, a complaint against an insurer where the consideration paid is Rs 1.2 crore must be filed before:
o: The State Commission, whose pecuniary jurisdiction is above Rs 50 lakh up to Rs 2 crore
e: After the 2021 Rules, the District Commission handles up to Rs 50 lakh, the State Commission above Rs 50 lakh up to Rs 2 crore, and the National Commission above Rs 2 crore.

t: Section 49 of the Insurance Act 1938 restricts a life insurer from declaring dividends to shareholders unless:
o: It has distributed bonus to all policyholders in the preceding year
The actuarial valuation shows a surplus and any share of surplus to shareholders does not exceed prescribed limits
It has been in business for at least 20 years
e: Section 49 restricts distribution of surplus to shareholders out of life funds except out of an actuarially certified surplus, and within limits determined by the Act and IRDAI.

t: Under the IRDAI (Re-insurance) Regulations 2018, every Indian insurer is required to maintain a minimum retention within India commensurate with its financial strength; the objective of the regulations is to:
o: Maximise retention within India and develop adequate reinsurance capacity, while ensuring the security of reinsurance arrangements
Transfer all risks to GIC Re
e: Regulation 3 sets out objectives including maximising retention within the country, developing adequate capacity and securing the best possible protection at a reasonable cost.

t: Under Section 2(7A) of the Insurance Act 1938 (as amended in 2015 and 2021), an 'Indian insurance company' must satisfy which of the following conditions?
o: It must be a company incorporated outside India but with a branch in India
It must be a company formed and registered under the Companies Act with foreign investment not exceeding 74% of paid-up equity
It must be wholly owned by Indian promoters with no foreign shareholding
It must be a cooperative society registered under State law
e: Section 2(7A) defines an Indian insurance company as a company formed under the Companies Act, with aggregate foreign investment not exceeding the prescribed limit, which is 74% after the Insurance (Amendment) Act 2021.

t: Under the Insurance Brokers Regulations 2018, an insurance broker must maintain professional indemnity insurance with a minimum limit of indemnity of:
o: Twice the annual remuneration received in the preceding year, subject to prescribed minimum amounts for each category
e: Brokers must hold PI cover with a limit of indemnity of at least twice the preceding year's remuneration, subject to minimum floors (e.g. Rs 1 crore for direct brokers).

t: Under the IRDAI Registration of Indian Insurance Companies Regulations 2022, which of the following businesses may a single insurer carry on under one registration?
o: Life insurance only, general insurance only, health insurance only, or reinsurance only; composite life-general registration is not permitted
General insurance and pension fund management together
e: The Act and regulations permit registration for one class of business: life, general, health or reinsurance; a composite licence for life and general is not currently permitted (though proposed in the 2024 Bill).

t: A corporate agent (a bank) proposes to tie up with 7 life insurers and 5 general insurers. Under the current Corporate Agents Regulations (as amended in 2022), this arrangement is:
o: Permitted only if IRDAI grants exemption
Not permitted, as the limit is 3 insurers per line
Permitted, as the limit is now a maximum of 9 insurers per line of business
Permitted only for banks with over 1,000 branches
e: The 2022 amendment raised the ceiling to 9 insurers in each of life, general and health lines (from 3 earlier), subject to board-approved policy.

t: Under the IRDAI AML/CFT Master Guidelines 2022, which of the following is a permitted mode of KYC verification for insurance customers?
o: Only physical verification of originals at a branch
Aadhaar-based e-KYC, Digital KYC, Video-based Identification Process (VBIP), OTP-based e-KYC and CKYC identifier, in addition to document-based KYC
e: The 2022 guidelines permit multiple KYC modes including Aadhaar OTP/biometric e-KYC, Digital KYC, VBIP and use of CKYC records, subject to PML Rules.

t: The National Insurance Academy (NIA), the apex training and research institute for the insurance industry promoted by LIC, GIC and the public sector general insurers, is located at:
e: NIA was established in 1980 at Pune by LIC, GIC and the four public sector general insurers to provide management training, education and research for the insurance industry.

t: Under IRDAI health insurance norms (2024), the cumulative premium under a health policy with multiple insurers can be claimed by the policyholder:
o: Only through the TPA appointed by IRDAI
Only from the insurer whose policy was issued first
From any one insurer chosen by the policyholder, with the balance claimable from the other insurer(s) for the unpaid amount
e: The policyholder with multiple indemnity policies may choose the insurer to settle the claim; the chosen insurer settles as per terms and the balance can be claimed from the other insurer(s).

t: Under the Agents Regulations 2016, an insurer must maintain a register of agents and must upload details of agent appointments on:
o: The IRDAI Agency Portal (centralised database) within a prescribed period
e: Insurers must update appointment and termination details on the IRDAI centralised agency database/portal, which also facilitates issuance of the unique agent identification.

t: 'Bima Sugam', envisaged under the IRDAI (Bima Sugam - Insurance Electronic Marketplace) Regulations 2024, is:
o: A digital public infrastructure/online marketplace for buying, selling, servicing insurance and settling claims across all insurers and intermediaries
A replacement for the Insurance Ombudsman
A Government subsidy scheme for crop insurance
e: Bima Sugam is an electronic insurance marketplace set up as a not-for-profit company with shareholding by life and general insurers, to serve as a one-stop platform for policyholders.

t: Under the IRDAI Master Circular on Health Insurance Products 2024, the maximum waiting period that an insurer may impose for specified diseases/procedures (other than PED) is:
e: The 2024 master circular limits waiting periods for PED and specified diseases/procedures to a maximum of 36 months (reduced from 48 months).

t: 'Bima Vistaar' refers to:
o: A composite, simple, affordable insurance product combining life, personal accident, property/dwelling and hospital cash cover for rural households
e: Bima Vistaar is IRDAI's proposed all-in-one affordable product (life, PA, property, hospital cash) for rural and underserved segments, part of the 'Insurance for All by 2047' vision.

t: Under the current IRDAI agent regulations (as revised in 2024 for ease of doing business), the earlier requirement of 25 hours of practical training before the IC-38 examination:
o: Was done away with, with the examination remaining mandatory
Was replaced by a 100-hour online course
e: The IRDAI (Insurance Intermediaries Registration/Agents) revisions of 2024 removed the prescribed pre-recruitment training hours while retaining the pre-recruitment examination.

t: Under the Micro Insurance Regulations 2015, a micro-insurance agent may be appointed by how many insurers?
o: One life insurer, one general insurer and one health insurer (or the Agriculture Insurance Company)
e: A micro-insurance agent may work with one life insurer, one general insurer and one standalone health insurer (plus the Agriculture Insurance Company of India).
